title: Scotch Game: Scotch Gambit
line: White brings the bishop out before taking the pawn back, and offers more if Black is greedy.

steps.text: The Scotch Game: Black has taken your pawn on d4.
Do not take back yet. Bring the bishop out, aimed at f7.

also.f3d4: Taking back is the Scotch Game itself, in other lessons. This lesson brings the bishop out.

steps.after: This is the Scotch Gambit. Black guards the pawn with its bishop.

steps.text: Offer a second pawn: move the pawn on c2 one square.
steps.after: Black takes it, a slip common at club level. Masters bring the knight out instead. The pawn on d4 no longer blocks your queen.

steps.text: That slip opens a line for your queen. Take on f7 with check: the king has to take the bishop.
steps.after: You gave the bishop for a pawn, but the king has come out.

steps.text: Check with the queen. She also attacks the bishop on c5.
steps.hint: The queen has an open line to the middle of the board.

steps.text: Take the bishop with check. You have the piece back.
Trade queens with check. Black has to take back, and then the pawn on c3 is yours.
Take back the pawn on c3 with the knight, which comes out at the same time.
steps.after: Material is level, and Black's king can no longer castle. That is what the greedy pawn grab cost.

summary: White develops before taking the pawn back. If Black grabs a second pawn, the check on the weak pawn wins time.
